_comment: Origin stories: the someone the captain met the night they took the ship (data/events/night.json, by background), whose story finds them in the first weeks. Each act 1 is chain_only, queued from the night with that person's role. Story definitions in data/stories.json. See docs/events.md.

warrant_posted.title: A warrant
warrant_posted.text: A handbill on the harbour wall in {port}: a warrant for mutiny and the theft of a King's sloop, signed by Captain {hunter} of the {nation_adj} navy. The lieutenant you locked in the cable tier has been given a ship of their own, and one order. Someone has been asking after the {ship}.

choices.text: Tear it down and find out who posted it
choices.result: A customs clerk, paid to remember, remembers: {hunter} will be back within the month, and wants to talk before hanging you.
choices.fail_result: Nobody will say. By evening all of {port} knows the {ship} is wanted, and by whom.

choices.text: Let it be known you'll kill whoever comes for you
choices.result: You say it in the loudest tavern in {port}. It will reach {hunter}. You meant it to.

choices.text: Leave it. Old paper, old crimes
choices.result: Old paper. But someone put up new copies.

warrant_frigate.title: {hunter}'s pennant
warrant_frigate.text: A frigate has been in the offing since dawn, and she's closing: {hunter}'s pennant at the masthead, {nation_adj} colours at the peak. She means to take you.

choices.text: Clear for action
choices.result: The drums beat to quarters. So be it.

choices.text: Run, and lose her among the cays
choices.result: You take the {ship} through a channel no frigate would dare. By nightfall she's gone. A week later, a note: {hunter} wants to talk.
choices.fail_result: She's faster than she looks. Her bow chasers find your range.

choices.text: Signal your old ship's number, and ask for a parley
choices.result: A long silence on the frigate's deck. Then the answering signal: tomorrow, in port, alone.

warrant_meet.title: Across the table
warrant_meet.text: {hunter} sits down across your table in {port}, alone, the sword left at the door. "I've read your file a hundred times. Tell me why I shouldn't hang you."

choices.text: Tell them the truth, all of it
choices.result: {hunter} listens to the end, then tears the warrant in half and leaves without a word.
choices.fail_result: "That's what they all say." {hunter} stands. "Next time, at sea."

choices.text: Buy the warrant (300 gold)
choices.result: Even honest officers have debts. This one had a lot.

choices.text: Follow them out and settle it in the alley
choices.result: It's quick. It's not clean. The {nation_adj} navy will want to know who did it.

warrant_taken.title: {hunter} in irons
warrant_taken.text: They bring {hunter} aboard in irons, bloody and furious, and stand them at the mast. Your crew want a hanging.

choices.text: Hang them from your yardarm
choices.result: The {nation_adj} navy will never forgive it. The crew will never forget it.

choices.text: Put them ashore with their sword
choices.result: {hunter} goes down the side without looking back. You'll never know if it was the right thing.

choices.text: Make them write home that you drowned
choices.result: {hunter} writes it, hand shaking. Officially, you're dead.
choices.fail_result: {hunter} spits on the paper. In the end you put them ashore anyway.

warrant_beaten.title: A promise
warrant_beaten.text: {hunter} stands on your quarterdeck with your colours over one arm. "I've no room for prisoners. Next time, it's a rope." Then they go back to their own ship and leave you drifting.

choices.text: Swallow it
choices.result: Your crew saw it all.

brand_catcher.title: The mark
brand_catcher.text: A runaway notice on the harbour wall in {port}: a description, a reward and a name: yours. {master} still holds your indenture, with years left to serve and every day you've been gone added on, and wants the sloop back too. The runaway's mark on your shoulder matches the notice.

choices.text: Find the bounty man before he finds you
choices.result: The bounty man won't be catching anyone for a while. But {master} will send another.

choices.text: Pay him to report you dead (120 gold)
choices.result: He takes the money and, for all you know, the next offer too.

choices.text: Lie low and sail at dawn
choices.result: You leave {port} in the dark, like the last time you ran.

brand_ship.title: Bound for {town}
brand_ship.text: A ship bound for {town}, low in the water. Not with sugar. With people, chained below, bought on the African coast for {master}'s fields. You worked those fields beside people who came the same way. Your contract had an end; theirs never will. Your crew are looking at you.

choices.text: Take her, and strike off their irons
choices.result: You run up your colours and go in.

choices.text: Let her go. You can't free them all
choices.result: You watch her out of sight. It doesn't get easier.

brand_freed.title: Irons by the rail
brand_freed.text: The irons are in a heap by the rail. The people who were in the hold stand on your deck in the sun and look at the coast, then at you. {freed} speaks for them, in the trade Portuguese of the African coast, and asks what you mean to do with them. {master} will hear of this by the next packet.

choices.text: Offer them a place under the articles
choices.result: {freed} and some of the others make their marks on the articles, for a full share like anyone. The rest ask to be put ashore, and you put them where they ask.

choices.text: Ask {freed} where they want to go, and take them
choices.result: Most want the hills, where the runaways live free; a few want any port with a ship bound for home. Three days out of your way. Nobody aboard complains.

brand_lost.title: Beaten off
brand_lost.text: The slaver's guns were heavier than they looked. She sails on for {town} with everyone still aboard, and {master} will know who tried.

choices.text: Next time
choices.result: Next time.

brand_master.title: A letter from {master}
brand_master.text: A lawyer finds you in {port} with a letter from {master}: "Come home, and I will be merciful. Stay away, and I will buy every warrant in the islands."

choices.text: Burn it in front of the lawyer
choices.result: The lawyer watches it curl up and goes to write a report.

choices.text: Buy your own papers, at a planter's price (250 gold)
choices.result: You find the one clerk in {town} who can be bought, and buy out your own indenture.

choices.text: Write back: one day you'll come for them
choices.result: You write it in a careful hand, so there's no mistaking it.

partner_letter.title: A letter from a gaol
partner_letter.text: A letter, smuggled out of the gaol in {town} and passed hand to hand until it found you in {port}. {partner} held the quay so you could get away, and they've hung everything you ever did on {partner} too. The rope is set for two months from now. They don't ask you for anything. That's the worst part.

choices.text: Set a course for {town}
choices.result: You show the letter to nobody, and give the navigator a new course.

choices.text: Send money for a lawyer (200 gold)
choices.result: A good lawyer. You'll never know if it was enough.

choices.text: Burn it
choices.result: It burns like any other letter.

partner_gaol.title: The gaol at {town}
partner_gaol.text: The gaol in {town} is an old powder store with a bored sentry and a padlock. Through the grating, {partner} sees you, and laughs, and can't stop.

choices.text: Bribe the gaoler (150 gold)
choices.result: The padlock turns out to have a key after all.

choices.text: Break them out tonight
choices.result: The sentry wakes up tied to his own musket. You're at sea by dawn.
choices.fail_result: The garrison turns out. You barely get yourself away. They hang {partner} the next morning, early, so you can't try again.

choices.text: Talk to the governor, and make them a deal
choices.result: It takes an evening, a promise and a lot of the governor's wine. {partner} walks out through the front door.

choices.text: Walk away
choices.result: You don't look back at the grating.

promise_letter.title: A lamp in the window
promise_letter.text: A letter waits for you at the harbour office in {port}, in a hand you'd know anywhere: {dear}, who stood on the quay with a lantern the night you left. They've taken a house in {town}, where the {ship} is bound to put in one day. They're still waiting. They want to know if they should.

choices.text: Write back: wait. You're coming home rich
choices.result: You write it three times before it sounds true. The crew notice you whistling.

choices.text: Write back: don't wait
choices.result: The kindest thing you've done in years. It doesn't feel like it.

choices.text: Don't answer
choices.result: You put it in your coat. You'll answer it tomorrow.

promise_home.title: {dear}
promise_home.text: {dear} is at the door before you've knocked. Older. So are you. "Well? Is it over?"

choices.text: Buy the house on the hill (800 gold)
choices.result: Not over. But there's a house now, and a lamp in its window, and you'll come home between voyages. That's a kind of promise.

choices.text: Bring {dear} aboard
choices.result: "I thought you'd never ask." {dear} has a sea chest packed already.

choices.text: One more voyage
choices.result: {dear} closes the door very gently.

promise_married.title: A letter from {town}
promise_married.text: A letter from {town}. {dear} has married a chandler. They wish you well, and mean it, and you wish they didn't.

choices.text: Drink to them
choices.result: The whole crew drinks to {dear}, whoever that is.

choices.text: Burn it
choices.result: You're short with everyone for a week.
